title: Our Home: Earth, a Unique Life Sustaining Planet

topics.title: What makes life possible on Earth

learn.hook: Venus is hotter than an oven and Mars is a freezing desert. Earth, the third planet from the Sun, is 'just right'. Out of all the planets we know, only Earth is known to have life!
points: Earth is at a suitable distance from the Sun, so it is neither too hot nor too cold, and water can stay liquid on its surface.
Liquid water covers about 71% of Earth's surface. All living things need water. But about 97% of Earth's water is salty sea water, and most fresh water is frozen as ice.
Earth's atmosphere gives us oxygen to breathe and carbon dioxide for plants. It also traps some heat, keeping Earth's average temperature comfortable, about 15 °C.
The ozone layer high in the atmosphere absorbs most of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet (UV) rays.
Earth also has fertile soil for plants, and a magnetic field that helps shield it from harmful particles streaming from the Sun.

example.q: Think it through: Why is liquid water so important when scientists search for life on other planets?
steps: Every living thing on Earth needs water to survive.
Water dissolves nutrients and carries them in living bodies.
So a planet with liquid water is more likely to support life as we know it.
example.answer: All known life needs liquid water, so it is one of the first things scientists look for.

learn.reallife: ISRO's Chandrayaan-1 mission (2008) helped find signs of water on the Moon, showing how important the search for water is in space science.

topics.title: Our air and the ozone shield

learn.hook: Every breath you take is a mixture of gases, and only about one-fifth of it is the oxygen your body needs!
points: Air is a mixture of gases: about 78% nitrogen, about 21% oxygen, and about 1% other gases such as argon, carbon dioxide and water vapour.
Oxygen is used by most living things to get energy from food. Carbon dioxide, though only about 0.04% of air, is used by plants to make food.
Some gases, like carbon dioxide and methane, trap heat. This natural greenhouse effect keeps Earth warm, but adding too much of these gases is warming Earth more and changing the climate.

The ozone layer can be damaged by chemicals called CFCs, once used in old refrigerators and sprays. Countries agreed in the Montreal Protocol (1987) to phase them out, and the ozone layer is slowly recovering.
Burning fuels, smoke from vehicles and burning waste pollute the air and can harm our lungs. Clean air is essential for good health.

example.q: Think it through: If air contains about 21% oxygen, how many litres of oxygen are in 100 litres of air?
steps: 21% means 21 parts out of 100.
21% of 100 litres = 21 litres.

learn.reallife: During winter, cities in north India sometimes face heavy smog. Air Quality Index (AQI) boards and apps help people know when to stay indoors.

learn.hook: There is no Planet B! But small daily choices, like carrying a cloth bag, can add up to a big difference for Earth.
points: Earth faces problems like air and water pollution, plastic waste, cutting of forests, loss of wild species and climate change.
Biodiversity means the variety of living things in a place. Protecting it keeps ecosystems healthy and balanced.
India protects wildlife through national parks, wildlife sanctuaries and biosphere reserves. Project Tiger, started in 1973, helped protect tigers and their forests.
Communities have also protected nature. In the Chipko movement of the 1970s in the Himalayan region, villagers hugged trees to stop them from being cut.
We can help by following the 3Rs: Reduce, Reuse, Recycle; by saving water and electricity, segregating wet and dry waste, planting native trees, and using public transport or cycling.

example.q: Think it through: Your family uses about 5 plastic bags a day. If you switch to cloth bags, how many plastic bags will you avoid in one week?
steps: Bags per day = 5
Days in a week = 7

learn.reallife: Many Indian cities ask homes to give wet waste and dry waste separately. Wet waste can become compost and dry waste can be recycled.

teach.ask: Gappu sighs: My tree is getting cut and the river smells funny. How can kids like you help protect Earth?

teach.nudge: What are the 3Rs? And what can we do about trees, wildlife and pollution?

revise.summary: Earth faces pollution, plastic waste, deforestation, species loss and climate change. Biodiversity keeps ecosystems healthy. India protects wildlife in national parks, sanctuaries and biosphere reserves; Project Tiger began in 1973 and the Chipko movement saved trees. We help through the 3Rs.
remember: Chipko (1970s, Himalayan region): villagers hugged trees
3Rs: Reduce, Reuse, Recycle; e.g. 5 bags a day × 7 = 35 bags saved a week
traps: Reusing a jar is reuse, not recycling
Burning garbage pollutes; it does not enrich the soil
Idling engines and driving alone increase pollution
